description: Somos estudiantes de cuarto año de Ingeniería Civil Industrial, interesados en la gestión de proyectos, el análisis y visualización datos y la resolución de problemas. Nos motiva enfrentar desafíos reales, tomar decisiones fundamentadas y crear soluciones innovadoras. Invitamos a sumarse a Araucan-IA a personas con conocimientos en programación, software, diseño, inteligencia artificial, análisis de datos, o comunicación, y disposición para colaborar con creatividad e iniciativa.
summary: Araucan-IA is an interactive web platform designed to explore, analyze, and visualize historical thermal activity and wildfire records in the La Araucanía region, Chile, spanning over two decades of data (2000–2026).
details:
AraucanIA – Detailed Project Description

Wildfire Activity Monitoring, Analysis and Forecasting Platform for Chile

Ignacio Montoya, Jeremías Barros, Rafael Silva and Fernando Rodriguez

Problem

Satellites produce large volumes of active fire detections, but the raw datasets are hard to interpret when analyzed separately. Without an integrated system, identifying regional patterns, comparing periods, understanding the intensity of events and anticipating where activity may appear next is slow and complex.

Solution

AraucanIA is an interactive web platform that processes, visualizes and forecasts satellite wildfire detections across Chile. It combines two layers in a single Streamlit application:

  • Descriptive layer. MODIS and VIIRS detections are cleaned, merged and aggregated into 5 × 5 km grid cells. Users explore them on an interactive satellite map, where detections are shown by Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and cells by activity level, with region and date filters.
  • Predictive layer. A machine-learning model estimates, for every zone, the probability that a satellite will detect thermal activity in the next 24 hours, shown next to live temperature, humidity and wind.

How It Works

  1. Data collection: NASA FIRMS active fire datasets from MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21).
  2. Cleaning and integration: Python and Google Colab standardize and validate the data, keep only vegetation-fire detections, map confidence levels to common categories and remove duplicates.
  3. Spatial aggregation: Detections are grouped daily into 5 × 5 km cells with detection count and average, maximum and total FRP. Cells are labeled low, medium or high activity using FRP terciles.
  4. Regional classification: GeoJSON boundaries assign detections to Chilean regions.
  5. Forecasting model: A gradient boosting classifier (scikit-learn) is trained on 569 zones of 0.25° (about 28 km), using only information available up to the forecast day: recent activity, neighboring zones, seasonal history, day of the year and location. It is trained on data up to 2022 and tested from January 2023 to July 2026 against simple baselines.
  6. Visualization: Results are presented in the Streamlit application.

Main Features

  • KPIs: Total detections, average and maximum FRP, most active day, share of high-confidence detections, number of high-activity cells and most active year.
  • Interactive satellite map: Detections by intensity and cells by activity level, with toggleable layers and hover information.
  • Activity calendar and monthly/annual analysis: A monthly heatmap and comparisons of months and years against average activity.
  • 24-hour risk forecast: A map of Chile colored by risk level, a table of the twelve highest-risk zones with live Open-Meteo weather, a critical-conditions flag and a temperature chart per zone.
  • Replay mode and validation panel: Reruns the forecast on any historical date, compares it with what satellites detected the next day and shows how reliable the model has been.
  • Exports: Filtered data in CSV and exportable charts.

All descriptive indicators and charts update together when a region and date range are applied.

Benefits and Expected Impact

By integrating several satellite sources into one interface, AraucanIA reduces the complexity of working with raw datasets.

  • A clearer view of the geographic distribution of fire detections, regional and temporal patterns, and easier comparison across months and years.
  • A validated 24-hour estimate. On the test period the model reached an average precision of 0.28, against 0.19 for persistence and 0.11 for climatology. In zones with no recent activity it roughly doubles the climatology's precision (0.09 vs. 0.04).
  • Relevant indicators without processing raw data, plus downloadable data and charts for further research.

Project Goals

Our goal is an accessible, practical tool for understanding where and when fire activity is concentrated in Chile and where it is most likely to appear next, as a foundation for data-driven wildfire monitoring. Next steps: deploy the forecast page publicly, measure the contribution of NASA POWER meteorology, automate data updates, unify the model with the harmonized MODIS + VIIRS 5 km grid and feed real-time weather into it.

Responsible use. AraucanIA is an experimental prototype. Its activity classes and risk levels are relative to the processed dataset, predict satellite detections rather than confirmed wildfires, and must not be used as official warnings or for emergency decisions.

Technologies and Tools

  • Python, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy: Data processing, cleaning and numerical analysis.
  • GeoPandas, Shapely, PyProj, Fiona and GeoJSON: Geospatial processing, regional boundaries and grid cells.
  • scikit-learn: Gradient boosting model and validation.
  • Streamlit, Plotly, pydeck and Esri: Web application, charts, maps and satellite imagery.
  • NASA FIRMS, Open-Meteo and NASA POWER: Fire detections, live weather and historical meteorology.
